record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Compares dropout and non-dropout training, and tests explicit terms intended to reproduce dropout's effect, using test accuracy and test error.
record.gate_note: Rows report dropout-related test accuracy or test error, and a measured effective-neuron ratio under dropout. Condensation and effective-neuron results do not measure a listed version, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. Flatness comparisons do not test V7's specified magnitude-aware sharpness-to-generalization-gap ranking.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares dropout with no-dropout training using held-out image-classification accuracy, testing V6. It is not an original source for that version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors derive R1 and R2, identify R1 as a key contributor to dropout's generalization and flatness benefits, and find that R1 facilitates weight condensation. They propose that condensation, flatness, and generalization may be linked; they do not establish condensation as a universal cause of better generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The study tests dropout against no-dropout training and explicit approximations to dropout's implicit regularization. It does not compare all the original claim's regimes or conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effect varies by model and dataset: the test-accuracy difference is small for the FNN and VGG-9 comparisons, and larger for ResNet-20 and the transformer. The explicit R̃2 term is described as only marginally improving generalization compared with R1.

fits_no_version.finding: An explicit R1 penalty approximately reproduces dropout's classification accuracy; the explicit gradient-norm penalty produces only marginal gains.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout's derived R1 regularizer reproduces more of its generalization benefit than the tested gradient-norm penalty.

fits_no_version.finding: Transformer test accuracy on Multi30k rises from 34.7% without dropout to 49.3% with dropout.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout improves held-out translation accuracy in the tested transformer and training recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Dropout-trained ResNet-18 models have lower effective-neuron ratios in selected convolutional layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout promotes weight condensation in selected ResNet-18 layers during CIFAR-10 training.

fits_no_version.finding: Dropout produces flatter filter-normalized loss slices, and the R1 analysis predicts decreasing Hessian trace under specified assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout and its R1 regularizer promote flatter solutions under the study's flatness definitions.

fits_no_version.finding: Teacher-student regression experiments report better test error with dropout, including tanh networks with more samples than the teacher's six free parameters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout can improve generalization in the tested synthetic regression problems.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
record.problems: The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the tabulated accuracy comparisons. Several cited test-error and test-accuracy plots have no precise values stated in the text. The experiments use restricted training subsets for several comparisons, including the first 1000 or 2048 examples in reported settings.
record.rows_left_out: Other plot-based accuracy or error results are not extracted as separate rows where exact values and condition assignments are not stated in the text. Figure 8 and Appendix Fig. 17 report averages over 10 trials, but their exact plotted values are not given in text.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.

A systematic classifier training-set-size sweep establishing the very-small-data exception; excessive dropout causing underfitting; removing dropout and weight decay together with augmentation. The 1000-example MNIST and 2048-example CIFAR-10 comparisons test particular subset settings but do not establish a small-data threshold.

Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking train-test gaps against norm- and margin-based measures within a convolutional family. Filter-normalized loss slices and Hessian-trace arguments do not establish this ranking.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 provides no uncertainty estimates. The study reports benefits on restricted classifier training subsets, but this alone does not identify or refute a precise very-small-data boundary. Other plot-based results, including Figures 8 and 17, were declared in rows_left_out and are not missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization compared with generalization on natural labels.
Test error across widths beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers compared with SGD under different tuning budgets.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Small training-set regimes, excessive dropout causing underfitting, and removing dropout and weight decay together with data augmentation.
The specified magnitude-aware sharpness measure's ranking of train-test gaps against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing the most memorized training examples and comparing test-accuracy effects with random removals.
